title: Pride
text:
Angels dressed in gold, in purple and hyacinth.

Genius and love are easy duties.


I kneaded only clay and from it drew gold.


He carried in his gaze the spirit of the heart.

In Paris, his desert, living exposed to the weather,

Strong as a beast and free as a God.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fragmentary grandeur of pride, alchemy, Paris as desert, and godlike freedom.

title: The Wine of Lovers
text:
Today space is fabulous!

Without bit, spurs, or bridle,

Let us depart on the back of wine

To a divine and magical sky!


Like two angels tortured

By implacable fever,

In the morning crystal

Let us follow the mirage.


Rocking on the wing

Of the intelligent whirlwind

In a shared delirium,


Sister, who swims beside me,

We will flee without rest

To the paradise of my dreams.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the intoxicated flight of the lovers through wine, mirage, and shared delirium.

title: The End of the Day
text:
Under a pale light

Life runs, dances, and writhes,

Impure and shrill.

As soon as to the heavens


Joyous night ascends

And everything, even hunger, calms,

Hiding shame,

The Poet says to himself: "At last!


My vertebrae, like my soul,

Covet sweet repose;

Full of funereal dreams


I will lean back

And roll among your veils,

Oh refreshing darkness!"
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's relief at nightfall, when noisy life gives way to dark repose.

title: Epigraph for a Condemned Book
text:
Peaceful and bucolic reader,

Naive and sober good man,

Throw away this Saturnian book,

Melancholic and orgiastic.


If you did not study your rhetoric

With Satan, the cunning dean,

Throw it away! you will understand nothing

Or you will judge me hysterical.


But if, safe from spells,

Your gaze tempts the abyss,

Read me and you will know how to love me;


Curious soul who suffers

And goes in pursuit of your paradise,

Pity me!... Or I curse you!
editorial_note: The translation preserves Baudelaire's warning to the innocent reader and invitation to the abyss-seeking one.

title: Bad Luck
text:
To lift so great a weight

Your courage would be needed, Sisyphus!

Even when one devotes oneself to the work,

Art is long and Time is brief.


Far from famous tombs,

In an isolated graveyard,

My heart, muffled drum,

Goes beating funeral marches.


Many a gem sleeps hidden

In darkness and oblivion,

Untouched by picks or probes.


Many a flower sadly exhales

Like a secret its pleasant fragrance

In the deep solitudes.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Sisyphus image and the hidden gem/flower figures of unrecognized art.
